layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Potentiodynamic polarization experiments were performed in 0.1N hy-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: drochloric acid and in 1N sodium chloride with austenitic alloys containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 18 to 20% Cr, 13 to 39% Ni, 0 to 5% Mo, and balance Fe. The pitting poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tials varied consistently with alloy content and correlated well with the re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sults of exposure tests in 0.33M ferric chloride. Increasing the molybdenum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and nickel contents increased the resistance to pitting; however, decreasing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the carbon and nitrogen contents also increased the resistance to pitting.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Critical current densities for passivity decreased sharply at all nickel leveĪs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with increases in the molybdenum content.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: One of the most important contributions of molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum alloying additions to stainless steels is the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resulting increase in the resistance to pitting corro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion. Although this behavior has been known for a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: long time, very little quantitative information is avail-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: able. Recent work on potentiodynamic determination

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of pitting potentials (1-6) suggests that this technique

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should be very useful in determining the relative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting resistances of various alloys.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A study was undertaken to learn whether or not the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concept of a pitting potential is valid and useful in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characterizing the resistance to pitting corrosion of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdenum-containing stainless steels. Once the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: utility of the technique was established the next step

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was to determine in detail how variations in molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum content affect the resistance of various stainiess

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels to pitting in environments containing chlorides.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In achieving this goal, it seemed desirable to use

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels of widely differing nickel contents so

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that possible nickel-molybdenum interactions could be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detected.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Procedures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Two series of austenitic stainless steels, one con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taining about 13% nickel and the other 39% nickel,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were induction-melted in an argon atmosphere and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cast in air. Each series was prepared using the split

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heat technique. In this technique, the base composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is melted and part of the melt is cast into an ingot. To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the balance of the melt, the required molybdenum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addition is made and the next ingot is cast. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process is repeated until a series of the desired com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: positions is cast. By this procedure, the residual and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impurity elements, which were intended to be in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range commonly present in commercial stainless steels,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were held essentially constant within each series.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Three high-purity alloys were also prepared as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: separate heats by melting and casting in vacuum.

layout_dets.text: mask after the onset of pitting. For this reason the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: magnitude of the corrosion current after the onset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of pitting was not a reliable indicator of the degree

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of pitting corrosion. In a few tests, only crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion was observed, and no true pits appeared

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the free electrode surface. The data from these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tests were therefore rejected. No potential scan was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: continued more than 20 mv beyond the potential at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which passivity broke down, even if the breakdown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was due only to crevice corrosion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in 0.1N HCl (Table III). None of the high-purity

layout_dets.text: alloys exhibited a pitting potential less noble than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Measurements in 1M NaCl.—An experimental pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gram similar to that performed in 0.1N HCl was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: undertaken in 1.0M NaCl. The literature reports that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increasing the chloride ion concentration increases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the pitting susceptibility of stainless steels, but chang-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing the pH from 1 to 7 does not affect pitting poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tials (6). However, this increase in pH did suppress

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the critical current for passivity to such an extent that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it could not be precisely measured on many of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels tested. For this reason, the currents and po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tentials corresponding to the active-passive transition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are not reported.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In contrast to the behavior observed in 0.1N HCl, in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1M NaCl many specimens showed current blips at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentials lower than those at which continuous pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: occurred. Microscopic examinations of electrodes on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which momentary current increases had occurred

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: showed some very small pits. Thus, these current

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: blips appear to correspond to the initiation of a pit that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: then repassivates almost immediately. The pits thus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formed are quite small and do not grow. A similar

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phenomenon has been described by Schwenk (2).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To check the significance of these current blips,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some specimens were subjected to the usual potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scan until well-defined current pulses were obtained.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: At this point the scan was stopped, and the specimen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was held at a constant potential while the current

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was recorded. The current pulses continued, becoming

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: less frequent and smaller until they died away com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pletely in a few hours. Holding electrodes at constant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentials, above those at which repassivating pits

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formed, for at least 24 hr did not cause a pit to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: propagate in any case. It is possible that these re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passivating pits are associated with extremely small

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: regions of considerable composition differences from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the bulk composition and that after these regions are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: removed the pits are too small to propagate at the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential in question. Since this type of repassivating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pit did not always occur on a given electrode and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was never observed to lead to a propagating pit if the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential scan was stopped, the potential at which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pits not only initiated, but continued to grow was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taken as the most important pitting potential.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To determine the influence of scanning rate on these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: measurements, the 13.5% nickel steel containing 2.9%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdenum was studied at various scanning rates in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.0M NaCl. The results (Table IV) indicate that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting potentials tend to shift in the noble direction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results obtained on the 13.5% nickel austenitic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels confirm that 1.0M NaCl is indeed a more severe

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting electrolyte than 0.1N HCl. It is also clear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that increasing molybdenum content up to at least

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.5% improves pitting resistance of these alloys. How-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ever, at 3.9% molybdenum the pitting potential was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tending toward lower values.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The anomalous behavior of the 3.9% molybdenum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel may be related to its microstructure. Delta ferrite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is present in the alloys containing over 2.9% molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum, with the 3.9% molybdenum alloy containing an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: appreciable amount. It has been reported by others

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (7) that delta ferrite is detrimental to resistance to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion. All the 39% nickel alloys were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: completely austenitic.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results on the 39% nickel alloys were very

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: similar to those obtained in 0.1N HCl, i.e., 1% molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum was sufficient to prevent stable pit growth

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at potentials below the transpassive region. Thus,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: even 1M NaCl is not a severe enough test medium to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differentiate the behavior of the 1, 3, and 5% molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum alloys.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The behavior of the high-purity alloys in 1M NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was almost identical to that in 0.1N HCl. The molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum-free alloy showed a greater tendency toward

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting at potentials just below the onset of transpas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sivity (0.79v). The alloys containing 2.5 and 5% molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum were not pitted on scanning to 0.8v. Thus, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: superior resistance of the high-purity alloys to pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion is even more evident in lM NaCl than it was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in 0.1N HCl.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Exposure tests in FeCl3—Simple exposure tests

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may be expected to be comparable with the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: difference, since pH changes between 1 and 7 have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: little effect in NaCl solutions(6). The redox potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was 0.540v vs. SCE. As can be seen from Table V, a

layout_dets.text: It is well-known that edges in stainless steels, i.e.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more susceptible to pitting than is the rolling plane

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (2). Thus, the coupons that yielded only edge pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the exposure tests should be considered to corre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the controlled potential measurements.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These results show that the potentiodynamic scan-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ning technique can give useful information about the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relative pitting resistances of stainless steels. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it is also clear that the details of experimental pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cedure must be carefully controlled. In particular,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scanning rate was found to have a considerable in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fluence on the results obtained. The avoidance of cre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vice corrosion was also found to be essential for ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taining any information on pitting potentials.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Table V. Results of exposure of austenitic steels to 0.33M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results of the effects of different scanning rates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are at variance with results reported in the literature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for molybdenum-free stainless steel (4,6). It has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reported that faster scans give more noble pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentials, but the opposite was found in this work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on molybdenum-containing alloys. The observation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: made in the present studies can be rationalized by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assuming that the passive film thickens with time, at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a potential in the passive range. Thus the passive film

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: would be thicker the slower the speed of scanning. As

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the film thickness increases, a larger fraction of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential difference between metal and solution would

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be expected to occur within the film and thus not be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: available at the film-solution interface to assist in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entry of chloride ions into the film.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It has been found previously that for some stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel the passive film increases in stability, probably

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as a result of increasing thickness, as time at a given

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential in the passive range increases(8). The effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was observed to be somewhat more pronounced for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys with molybdenum than for those without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdenum, perhaps indicating that passive film

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thickening is more important when molybdenum is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: present in the alloys. A similar effect was reported by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Streicher (9), who found that passivation of type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 316 after pickling and before undergoing a pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test had a much larger beneficial effect than did a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: similar treatment of type 304. This reasoning is highly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: speculative, but may, at least in part, account for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contradiction between results from this work and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: those reported by others.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Even if absolute values of the pitting potential are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: open to question, it appears that relative pitting po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tentials provide useful information. In the two series

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of austenitic alloys investigated, increasing molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum content consistently increased the pitting po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tential except in the 13.5% nickel alloy of highest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdenum content. Here the occurrence of ferrite as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a second phase is promoted by higher molybdenum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content and complicates the situation by introducing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differences in composition, that is, the delta ferrite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: would be enriched in chromium and molybdenum and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depleted in nickel (10). In all other steels, the benefi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cial effect of increasing molybdenum content on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting potential was clearly revealed even when the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increments were as small as ½ %. That these variations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in pitting potential are significant was confirmed by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the good correlation obtained with the results of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exposure tests in FeClg. Of course, since pitting po-

layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The polarographic reductions of 1,8-dinitronaphthalene, 5,6-dinitroace-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: naphthene, 3,4-dinitroacenaphthenequinone, and 4,5-dinitronaphthalic an-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hydride, were studied in buffered solutions at four different pH values. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relative' wave heights of the multiple waves could be interprēted reasonably

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in terms of certain electron changes. A semi-empirical equation was derived

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to confirm certain electron changes in the polarographic reductions. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electron changes were also checked by coulometric measurements on elec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trolyses run at controlled potentials. Results indicated that in all but one in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stance there was agreement between the values for the electron changes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: obtained in the parallel analyses. The one exception was 3,4-dinitroacenaph-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thenequinone.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In general, the polarographic reduction of a poly-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitro aromatic compound proceeds in a stepwise man-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ner, and the first step corresponds to a four-electron

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: change. This has been interpreted as corresponding to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the reduction of one of the nitro groups to an hy-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: droxylamino group. In a study of the polarographic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reductions of the ten dinitronaphthalenes (1), the 1,8-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: isomer was the only compound that did not exhibit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this characteristic behavior. Instead it gave an initial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wave that corresponded to either an eight or ten-elec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tron change depending on the acidity of the solution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It was suggested that this might be due to the forma-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion of the ring compound 1,8-naphthopyrazole.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Thus far large-scale electrolyses of 1,8-dinitronaph-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thalene at controlled potentials have not yielded a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: product identifiable as perinaphthopyrazole, but have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instead yielded very high-melting, highly colored ma-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: terials which appear to be polymeric.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Grimshaw and Rea (2) have recently reported that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the electroreduction of 1-acetylnaphthalene did not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yield the expected pinacol in base, but gave an un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expected product due to coupling in the 4-position.
